findings.title: Calibration selector headlines a 9-option, single-expiry fit (2026-09-11) because thin data gives the lowest RMSE. This is the SPX-leg version of the C20 bug
findings.description: latest_good_calibration_path() ranks acceptable fits by minimum SPX RMSE. is_acceptable_calibration gates only on the VIX tenor count (>=3), with no check on the SPX leg. The calibrator takes 9 highest-vega strikes per expiry bucket (_CAL_STRIKES_PER_EXPIRY=9), so n_spx_options=9 means ONE expiry. Five Heston parameters fitted to one smile give a very low RMSE, so the selector now promotes joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl, the only fit made during the known daily-expiry outage, over every properly identified fit. The page shows SPX RMSE 0.215 vp with a green 'Good fit'. It also shows kappa=4.9997, Feller BINDING, 3 effective dof and 'Fit from 9 SPX options', and marks the n_SPX/n_VIX cell green. On a single expiry the kappa/theta term structure is not identified by the SPX leg at all. This is exactly the failure README section 'Why the headline fit is chosen on data sufficiency, not RMSE' claims is fixed, now happening on the SPX leg. It also breaks README's 'must match the dashboard' promise. The README showcase (2026-05-31: kappa=1.77, theta=0.067, sigma=0.46, RMSE 0.52, Feller PASS) has not matched the site since 2026-07-01: the selector picked 07-01 (kappa=2.22, 0.375 vp) from Jul 1 to Sep 10 and has picked 09-11 since. Min-RMSE 'best of archive' also mixes up freshness and quality. The index badge 'Calibration: <date>' sits next to 'Last close', but it is the date of the lowest-RMSE fit, which can be months old while newer good fits exist.
findings.evidence: Listed all pickles with is_acceptable_calibration: every 4-tenor fit from 06-16 to 09-04 has n_spx_options 36-54 (4-6 expiries), RMSE 0.375-2.8. joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl: 'rmse=0.215 nspx=9 nvix=4 ok=True'. Simulated the selector at different cutoffs: <=09-10 -> joint_cal_2026-07-01 {kappa 2.22, theta 0.058, sigma 0.427, spx 0.375, PASS, nspx 54}; <=09-24 -> joint_cal_2026-09-11 {kappa 5.0, theta 0.043, sigma 0.657, spx 0.215, BINDING, nspx 9}. load_page2 output: kappa=4.9997, spx_rmse=0.215, n_spx_options=9, effective_dof=3. The live index badge reads 'Calibration: 2026-09-11'. The known CI log for the same failure mode says 'SPX surface: 9 liquid options across 1 expiries'.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Record n_spx_expiries = spx_surface['time_to_expiry'].nunique() in JointCalibrator.calibrate()'s result. (2) Extend is_acceptable_calibration(params, rmse, n_vix_tenors, n_spx_expiries=None, n_spx_options=None) with _MIN_SPX_EXPIRIES=3 (4 is better). For legacy pickles, infer expiries = n_spx_options // 9 and reject n_spx_options < 27. Apply this at write time (cloud_refresh) and at selection time (app.py:80). (3) Change the selection policy to the NEWEST acceptable fit, i.e. max spot_date or as_of_date, and return (path, reason, age_sessions). If a pinned reference fit is wanted for README, add an explicit SHOWCASE constant and label it 'reference fit' on the page. (4) Generate the README 'showcase' block from the same function, or reword it to say the dashboard shows the latest accepted fit. Tests: build a tmp calibrations dir with a 9-option fit at RMSE 0.2 and a 54-option fit at RMSE 0.5. The selector must return the 54-option fit. The 09-11 pickle must fail is_acceptable_calibration.

findings.title: PDV spread percentile counts 4,125 NaN rows as 'not below': live site says '1.1th percentile, vol cheap' when the NaN-excluded value is the 75th
findings.description: pdv_spread_pct = (hist_spread_pp < cur_spread).mean() over regime_labels.parquet. That parquet has feature values for only the 64 rows the daily bot appended (2026-06-22..2026-09-23); the other 4,125 rows have NaN pdv_iv_spread. NaN < x is False, so the percentile is divided by 4,189 rows instead of 64, which pins it near 0. The page then shows the blue 'Spread at 1.1th percentile — vol appears cheap relative to 10-year history' box. Right beside it the page says 'Historical mean +4.06pp. Current +6.81pp', which contradicts the percentile on sight. With NaNs excluded the percentile is 75.0 (84.4 on the local DB), which is near the amber 'premium selling regime' threshold of 80, so the conclusion flips. Three more errors: (a) the 'history' is 64 days, not the '2015–2025' / '10-year' the template hard-codes. (b) The historical rows are rv_20d − VIX, because cloud_refresh calls build_features without a pdv_model, while the current value is VIX − PDV forecast. Two different quantities are ranked against each other. (c) pdv_spread_mean (+4.06) is the mean of those 64 rv-based rows.
findings.evidence: python: rl=pd.read_parquet('data_store/signals/regime_labels.parquet'); rl.isna().sum() gives vix..vvix 4125 each; first non-null row 2026-06-22, count 64. For cur=6.81 (live): dashboard pct=1.1, NaN-excluded pct=75.0, n_hist=64, span 2026-06-22..2026-09-23. For cur=8.03 (local): 1.3 vs 84.4. Live page text (curl navnoorbawa.me): 'IMPLIED − REALISED SPREAD +6.81pp ... 1.1th percentile 2015–2025 mean: +4.06pp ⓘ Spread at 1.1th percentile — vol appears cheap relative to 10-year history. Historical mean: +4.06pp . Current: +6.81pp'.
findings.proposed_fix: Build a like-for-like history in load_page1: pred = pdv.linear_.predict(pdv._features[['sigma1','sigma2','lev']]) over 2010+, joined with vix_daily closes from the DB, then spread_t = VIX_t − 100·pred_t. Better still, recompute the features to the current session (see the stale-PDV finding). Compute pct = (hist.dropna() < cur).mean(). Derive the label window from hist.index.min()/max() and remove the hard-coded '2015–2025' and '10-year' text. Show n_obs. Fix the ordinal ('75th', not '75.0th'). Test: a parquet with NaN history must give the same percentile as the NaN-dropped series, and a current value above the mean must give a percentile above 50.

findings.title: Headline PDV forecast is frozen at 2025-12-30 features and paired with today's VIX, and the C21 'pdv_stale' flag is computed but never rendered
findings.description: load_page1 takes pdv._features.iloc[-1] from the pickled model. Those features end 2025-12-30, and the daily bot never refits the model or commits pdv_model.pkl. The page's biggest numbers, 'PDV FORECAST (REALISED) 8.37%' and 'IMPLIED − REALISED SPREAD +6.81pp' with 'Moderate vol risk premium → favours short vol strategies', therefore subtract a nine-month-old one-day-ahead forecast from the 2026-09-23 VIX. Commit 75b4844 (C21) says the PDV card 'now stamps the feature date and flags staleness'. The code computes d['pdv_stale']=True, but no template references pdv_stale, so nothing is flagged. The only hint is 'Updated: 2025-12-30' in 11px grey text. The regime classifier's pdv feature and the sparkline are inconsistent with this frozen value as well.
findings.evidence: pdv_model.pkl: _features index 2010-01-05..2025-12-30. load_page1: pdv_date='2025-12-30', pdv_stale=True. `grep -c 'd.pdv_stale' dashboard/templates/*.html` returns 0 in every file. The live page shows 'PDV FORECAST (REALISED) 8.37% ... Updated: 2025-12-30' beside 'CURRENT VIX 15.18%' for 2026-09-23.
findings.proposed_fix: Recompute the forecast on every render from current data: r = log returns from spx_ohlcv up to spx_date; feats = extract_pdv_features(r); forecast = pdv.linear_.predict(feats[['sigma1','sigma2','lev']]).iloc[-1]. This takes milliseconds and uses fitted coefficients only, so there is no look-ahead. Set pdv_date to the last feature date and render a visible amber banner when pdv_date < spx_date. Optionally refit PDV yearly in CI. Test: monkeypatch the DB to end on date X and assert pdv_date == X. Also assert that a stale pickle renders the banner text.

findings.title: `python dashboard/app.py` (the README quickstart) overwrites the tracked regime_labels.parquet with the demoted classifier's predictions, undoing the C21 fix
findings.description: _startup_data_refresh runs in a daemon thread when app.py is started directly. It fires whenever the SPX data is more than 3 days old, which is always true on a fresh clone because the tracked vol_system.db ends 2026-06-18. It calls DataPipeline.daily_refresh(), which writes to the tracked DB, and then _refresh_regime_labels(). That function writes clf.predict_series(feats) (the XGBoost classifier that C17 demoted) over the entire regime_labels.parquet. This is exactly what commit 90dc851 removed from cloud_refresh ('publish rule labels ... not classifier output'). The front page then headlines those predictions under 'Deterministic rule — the label the backtest trades on', and a later `git commit -a` would publish them. The 4-hour scheduled refresh repeats the overwrite. Meanwhile, under the documented server entry point (Procfile: gunicorn dashboard.app:app) the __main__ block never runs, so both threads, and their 'Railway health-check' rationale, are dead code in production.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy, called m._refresh_regime_labels() (DB-only, no network). before=(4189 rows, 2010-01-26..2026-09-23), after=(4088 rows, 2010-02-02..2026-06-18). Label agreement on common dates was 67.7% of 4088. 101 dates were lost. R2 share went from 21.8% to 40.9%. `git status` showed ' M data_store/signals/regime_labels.parquet'. app.py:1210 `labels = clf.predict_series(feats.dropna())`; app.py:1215 `rl.to_parquet(out_path)`.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete _refresh_regime_labels, _startup_data_refresh and _scheduled_data_refresh and the thread start-up. The site is built by the daily CI job, and a display layer must never write to data_store. If a local refresh is wanted, add a `--refresh` CLI flag that calls scripts/cloud_refresh.refresh_market_data() + extend_regime_labels() (the rule-label path) and writes to a git-ignored location. Add a test that imports dashboard.app, calls every load_page*, then runs `git status --porcelain data_store` and asserts it is empty. Add a test that app.py source contains no 'predict_series' or '.to_parquet('.

findings.title: Front page depends on unpickling the research-only classifier: a bad pickle gives HTTP 500 and blocks the deploy, and missing rule labels make the page headline classifier output as the 'rule label'
findings.description: The headline rule regime and the regime-frequency stats are computed inside the same try-block that unpickles regime_classifier.pkl. (1) If the pickle fails to load, the except-branch never sets reg*_n or reg_total. The template then calls "{:,}".format(Undefined) and raises TypeError, so '/' returns 500 and freeze_site exits 1. cloud_refresh then calls sys.exit(1) and the whole day's deploy is skipped because of a component labelled 'not used for trading'. This is a live risk: requirements are unpinned (scikit-learn>=1.3, xgboost>=2.0), and loading already emits InconsistentVersionWarning (pickled with sklearn 1.7.1, loaded with 1.9.1) plus an XGBoost 'serialized model from older version' warning. (2) In the same failure branch the classifier card shows the rule label as the classifier's call, with made-up 100/0/0 probability bars. (3) If regime_labels.parquet is missing or unreadable, line 286 sets `reg = clf_reg`, so the page headlines the classifier prediction under 'Current Regime — rule-based label' (then crashes on reg_total).
findings.evidence: Scratch-copy experiments. Wrote garbage to regime_classifier.pkl: load_page1 gave regime_error='pickle data was truncated', prob_r1=100.0, clf_conf=0, reg_total=None, and render_template gave 'TypeError unsupported format string passed to Undefined.__format__'; test_client GET / returned 500. Moved regime_labels.parquet away: load_page1 gave regime_label='R2', regime_name='VOMMA ACTIVE' (= clf_label R2, 70.0%), reg_total=None, and GET / returned 500. pip list: scikit-learn 1.9.1, xgboost 3.2.0; warnings seen at load.
findings.proposed_fix: Split load_page1 into independent blocks. The rule regime and frequencies read only regime_labels.parquet; if it is missing, show 'Rule label unavailable' and never fall back to the classifier. The classifier card lives in its own try/except and hides itself on failure. Give reg*_n/reg_total explicit None defaults and make the template tolerate None (`{% if d.reg_total %}`). Pin scikit-learn/xgboost to the versions that produced the pickle, or re-save the XGBoost model with Booster.save_model and load it version-independently. Tests: parametrize over {corrupt classifier, missing labels}. Assert GET / returns 200, the headline equals the parquet's last rule label (or 'unavailable'), and it is never the classifier output.

findings.title: Research-only classifier card gets inconsistent features: pdv_iv_spread is always −VIX because the PDV forecast is computed later, and the RV definitions differ from training
findings.description: feat_live is built at line 257 with pdv_dec = d.get('pdv_forecast') / 100, but d['pdv_forecast'] is only set at line 386. The feature is therefore pdv_iv_spread = 0 − VIX, for example −0.164 instead of about −0.05. This is the classifier's second most important feature (24.7% importance). The other features also depart from training: rv uses the sample std of simple returns (pct_change().std()) where training uses the root-mean-square of log returns, rv_change_5d uses std(last 5) − std(previous 5) where training uses rv5(t) − rv5(t−5), and the fear_premium clip is missing. The card's 'R2 · 70%' and the 'Classifier disagrees with the rule label' sentence are produced by this bug.
findings.evidence: On the local DB (as of 2026-06-18). dashboard feat_live: pdv_iv_spread=-0.164, fear_premium=0.9955. build_features(spx,vix,pdv_model) last row: pdv_iv_spread=-0.0515, fear_premium=1.0166. clf.predict_proba: dashboard [0.023,0.277,0.700] (R2); training-consistent with PDV [0.033,0.580,0.387] (R1). clf.feature_importance(): fear_premium 0.393, pdv_iv_spread 0.247.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not rebuild features by hand. Call feats = build_features(get_spx_ohlcv(as_of_date=spx_date), get_vix_term_structure_wide(...), pdv_model=pdv) and pass feats.iloc[[-1]] to clf.predict_proba. This is the same code path used for training. Test: assert that the probabilities load_page1 shows equal clf.predict_proba(build_features(...).iloc[[-1]]) to 1e-9.

findings.title: Calibration-page smile chart and the whole Greeks page come from a 2026-03-24 fit that the quality gate rejects (rho=−0.99, 3.83 vp, S=6581), shown under a 2026-09-11 / SPX 7657 header
findings.description: The 'SPX Implied Volatility Smile — All Maturities' chart on the calibration page is not the market smile and not the headline fit's smile. It is the iv column of greeks_surface.parquet, which holds Heston model IVs from joint_cal_2026-03-24 (kappa 4.62, rho −0.99, below today's −0.95 bound, SPX RMSE 3.83 > the 3.0 gate, Feller VIOLATED) at S=6581, r=4.5%, q=1.3%. The page header says '2026-09-11 · SPX = 7657.0 · r = 3.91%'. At 91 days the displayed smile is about 9 vol points above the headline fit's own smile. No market quotes are overlaid, although the README advertises an 'SPX smile overlay'. The entire Greeks Risk Monitor, including the unstable-node banner, vomma heatmap and vanna, comes from that same stale, gate-rejected surface. Its strikes (K=5034..7755) are relative to 6581, while spot is 7706 today. The header hard-codes '2026-03-24' (the parquet says 2026-03-25), '69 nodes' and 'All three unstable nodes are at the 1-year maturity'. The axis label ln(K/S) is wrong; the surface uses ln(K/F).
findings.evidence: compute_greeks_surface(S=6581, r=.045, q=.013, params of joint_cal_2026-03-24) reproduces parquet 91d IV [35.87, 34.58, ..., 20.08] to 0.01. The 09-11 headline fit gives 91d IV [26.28, 25.10, ..., 10.77]. K/exp(lm) gives an implied F of 6589 at 14d rising to 6795 at 365d, so lm is ln(K/F). The parquet as_of_date is 2026-03-25. Rebuilding the surface from the headline fit took 0.26 s and moves the unstable nodes to 60/180/365d at K≈8113-8970.
findings.proposed_fix: In load_page2/load_page3, load the selected calibration once (shared helper) and call compute_greeks_surface(cal['S'], cal['r_used'], cal['q_used'], cal['params']), which takes 0.26 s, or have CI rebuild greeks_surface.parquet after every accepted calibration. Store the market anchor points (K, T, market IV, model IV) in the calibration pickle at fit time. The CI DB is never committed, so the snapshot cannot be reloaded later. Plot market dots against model lines from those anchors. Render the as_of, S and n_nodes from the data and delete the hard-coded texts. Test: assert that the smile shown on the calibration page equals the Heston IV of the selected pickle's params and S to 1e-6, and that the greeks badge date equals the selected calibration's spot_date.

findings.title: 'Heston vs Quintic OU' table compares fits on different dates and datasets, which flips the sign of the SPX Δ
findings.description: spx_delta = quintic SPX RMSE (2026-03-24 surface) − headline Heston SPX RMSE, and the headline Heston fit is currently 2026-09-11 with 9 options. The table shows Quintic worse by +2.128 vp in red. The same-day Heston fit (joint_cal_2026-03-24, 3.833 vp, also stored in bates_cal['heston_comparison']) shows Quintic BETTER by −1.49 vp. VIX-futures Δ is likewise −0.265 displayed against −1.149 same-day. The card's own prose ('captures steep SPX left skew without rho saturating') contradicts the table. The Bates block computes the same cross-date deltas but is never rendered (dead code; it unpickles a 139 s fit on every request).
findings.evidence: quintic_cal_2026-03-24: spx 2.3427, vix_fut 0.0011. joint_cal_2026-03-24: spx 3.8334, vix_fut 1.1502. Headline 09-11: spx 0.215, vix_fut 0.266. load_page2: quintic.spx_delta=2.128, vix_delta=-0.265. bates_cal_2026-03-24 contains heston_comparison {'heston_spx_rmse': 3.8334, ...}.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare against the Heston fit from the same snapshot (load joint_cal_<quintic as_of>.pkl, or the stored heston_comparison) and print the snapshot date in the table header. Remove the unused Bates block or render it with the same-date Heston. Test: assert that the quintic delta uses a Heston pickle whose as_of_date equals the quintic file date.

findings.title: Calibration page shows r=3.91% and q=0.00%, but the fit used r=4.5% and q=1.3%
findings.description: cloud_refresh builds JointCalibrator(as_of_date=TODAY) with the defaults r=0.045 and q=0.013. calibrate()'s result dict records neither r nor q. cloud_refresh then writes result['r'] = get_tbill_rate(TODAY), a rate the fit never used. The dashboard displays that r (badge 'r = 3.91%', table 'Risk-free rate 3.91%', hard-labelled 'USD 6M SOFR (2026-03)'). Because q is absent, cal.get('q', 0) shows 'Dividend yield 0.00%'. The carry in the fit was 3.2%; the page implies 3.91%, so anyone repricing from the displayed parameters gets the wrong forward. Other hard-coded texts are stale in the same way: 'DE (120 iter × 40)' against the code default of 200 iterations × popsize 10, and the 'VIX Options RMSE' bar plots 0.0, so a disabled leg looks like a perfect fit.
findings.evidence: joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl keys: no 'q'; r=0.03913. load_page2: r_pct=3.91, q_pct=0.0. joint_calibrator.py:477-478 `r: float = 0.045, q: float = 0.013`; cloud_refresh.py:308 `JointCalibrator(as_of_date=TODAY)`, :315 `result['r'] = get_tbill_rate(TODAY)`. calibrate() defaults: de_maxiter=200, de_popsize=10.
findings.proposed_fix: Have calibrate() include 'r': self.r, 'q': self.q in its result. In cloud_refresh, pass r=get_tbill_rate(spot_date) (converted to continuous compounding) INTO the constructor and never overwrite afterwards. In app.py, display cal['r'] and cal['q'] and show 'unrecorded' when missing, not 0. Replace the SOFR label with the actual source (^IRX on spot_date). Hide the VIX-options bar or mark it 'disabled'. Test: the pickle's r and q equal JointCalibrator.r and .q. load_page2 shows q='—' when the key is absent.

findings.title: Loader failures are swallowed: no *_error key is ever rendered, so a missing Greeks surface shows a green '0 / 0 unstable' all-clear, a missing backtest shows NAV $0, and a missing calibration returns 500
findings.description: Every loader catches Exception and fills defaults (0, [], '2026-05-31', percentile 50, 'N/A'). No template references any of db_error/regime_error/pdv_error/cal_error/smile_error/greeks_error/eq_error/pkl_error/ann_error/wf_error, so a failure renders as plausible data. freeze_site only fails on status!=200 or a 'Traceback' string, so these pages deploy. Examples: (a) with the Greeks parquet missing, the risk monitor shows 'Unstable Nodes 0 / 0' with class 'card-value green', a false all-clear, above hard-coded '6 maturities · 2026-03-24' and 'Across all 69 nodes'. (b) With full_results.parquet missing: 'NAV: $0 · P&L: $+0', status 200. (c) With no calibration: cal_error sets kappa=0 and the template's 0.693/d.kappa*252 raises ZeroDivisionError (500). (d) Fallback dates such as calib_date '2026-05-31' and as_of '2026-05-31' present an invented date as data. There are no tests of dashboard/app.py or freeze_site.py anywhere in joint_vol_calibration/tests. The C21 commit says 'test_c21_audit_fixes.py pins every fix above', yet none of its dashboard fixes (regime frequencies, pdv_stale, n_trades) are tested.
findings.evidence: Scratch-copy scenarios with test_client: no_greeks -> /greeks 200 with text 'Unstable Nodes 0 / 0 ... Max Vomma 0 365d maturity nodes ... Across all 69 nodes', 'card-value green' present. no_bt -> /backtest 200 'NAV: $0 · P&L: $+0 ... 0 /0 negative'. no_cal -> load_page2 cal_error='No such file ... joint_cal_2026-05-31.pkl', and render gives 'ZeroDivisionError float division by zero'. `grep -rn load_page joint_vol_calibration/tests` finds no matches.
findings.proposed_fix: Collect errors into d['errors'] and render one red banner in base.html when it is non-empty. Use None, not 0, for missing numeric fields and have the templates show '—' (guard the half-life with `{% if d.kappa %}`). In freeze_site, fail the build (exit 1) when any loader reports an error or any page contains 'nan'/'None' in a numeric slot, and log which one. Add tests/test_dashboard.py: render all four routes with the shipped artifacts (200, no error banner). Parametrize artifact removal and assert a visible error banner rather than a 500 or zeros. Add the render test to tests.yml.

findings.title: No staleness signal for the calibration, PDV or Greeks inputs, the freshness badge never escalates, and the VIX term structure silently mixes dates
findings.description: The view-time freshness check looks only at spx_date. Any older date shows the same neutral '⟳ refreshes after next U.S. close', so a site stale for a month looks identical to one a few hours behind, and holidays are not handled. The live page right now shows a green '✓ latest U.S. session' next to 'Calibration: 2026-09-11', which is 9 sessions old during the known outage, and a PDV forecast from 2025-12-30 without any warning. The VIX term-structure query takes each ticker's own MAX(date). When the sub-tenor rows are missing for the latest session, which the README says happens routinely on Yahoo, the curve, the CONTANGO/BACKWARDATION label, the slope and the classifier's ts_slope combine today's VIX with older 9D/3M/6M values. The per-ticker dates (vix_date, vvix_date, ts_max_date) are computed for exactly this purpose and never rendered. In CI the DB restarts from the tracked 2026-06-18 file every run, so a missing sub-tenor day would pair today's VIX with June values.
findings.evidence: Playwright render of the live index: badge 'Last close: 2026-09-23 · Calibration: 2026-09-11 · Regime: 2026-09-23 · ✓ latest U.S. session'. Scratch DB truncated to <=2026-06-17 (sub-tenors missing 06-15..06-17): load_page1 gives vix=18.44 (06-17), ts_values=[17.26, 18.44, 20.51, 22.59] where the 9D/3M/6M values are from 2026-06-12, ts_regime=CONTANGO, ts_max_date=2026-06-17; the page never mentions 2026-06-12. yfinance today also returns a ^VIX row for 2026-09-07 (Labor Day) with no ^VIX3M/9D/6M/VVIX. `grep -c 'd.vix_date\|d.ts_max_date' templates` returns 0.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Server side, compute age in NYSE sessions (pandas_market_calendars or a holiday list) for spx_date, calib spot_date, pdv_date and the greeks as_of. Render amber at more than 1 session and red at more than 3, per item, in the badge. Make freeze_site exit non-zero, or at least emit a GitHub warning annotation, when the calibration is more than N sessions old. (2) Build the term structure from a single date: the latest date on which ^VIX, ^VIX3M and ^VIX9D all exist. If that date is older than the VIX date, show 'Term structure as of <date>'. (3) In the JS, show '⚠ n sessions stale' when the gap is more than 1. Tests: a fixture DB with missing sub-tenors must give a single-date curve plus the date label, and a calibration 10 sessions old must render the stale banner.

findings.title: 'Walk-Forward Sharpe — 6-Month OOS Windows' is in-sample, uses a flat 5% hurdle instead of the ^IRX path, and clips 7 of 13 bars at −4
findings.description: The chart slices the single full-period equity curve into half-years. Nothing is retrained, so these are in-sample sub-period Sharpes, not OOS walk-forward, even though the engine has a real walk_forward_validation() that retrains per window. The chart also subtracts a flat 5%/252, while the page headline and methodology row #9 say Sharpe is 'measured against the per-date ^IRX T-bill path instead of a flat 5%'. In 2020-2021 the T-bill yielded about 0.1% and the NAV is 73-97% flat, so the 5% hurdle alone produces −18 Sharpe (2020-H2), and 2020-H1/2022-H1 switch sign. Values are clipped to ±4 with no annotation, so 7 of 13 bars show exactly −4.0. The published '11/13 negative' becomes 9/13 with the T-bill hurdle. pct_change within each slice also drops the first day of every window.
findings.proposed_fix: Either run engine.walk_forward_validation() in the backtest job and persist wf_df to full_results.pkl for the dashboard to plot, or rename the chart 'Half-year sub-period Sharpe (in-sample)'. Use the ^IRX series from the DB (the same one compute_metrics uses) instead of 0.05/252. Compute each window's returns from the previous window's last NAV. Replace the clip with a log or symlog axis, or label clipped bars with their true value. Test: the window Sharpe on a synthetic NAV equals compute_metrics(sub, rf_series) to 1e-9, and no value is silently clipped.

findings.title: Portfolio KPI row 'N Trades 283 / Avg P&L per trade −$923 / Win Rate 28.16%' uses different definitions from the per-signal table (141 round trips) and the engine (292, −$1,806, 45.5%)
findings.description: C21 set out to replace an S1C-only transition count ('176 vs the real 141 round trips'). The replacement sums position-change events over s1c/s3/s4. An entry and an exit each count, as does any size change, so the total is 283, neither 141 nor the engine's 292. Avg P&L per trade (−$923) is therefore half the per-round-trip figure. 'Win Rate 28.16%' is the share of non-zero-P&L days that are positive, while the per-signal table immediately below reports win rate per trade (S1C 36.4%, S3 72.7%, S4 25.8%) and the engine's portfolio win_rate is 45.5%. The same page shows three definitions under one label.
findings.evidence: load_page4 metrics_rows: 'Win Rate 28.16%', 'Avg P&L / Trade $-923', 'N Trades 283'. full_results.pkl metrics: n_trades=292, avg_pnl_per_trade=-1805.63, win_rate=0.4555; s1c_n_trades 88 + s3 22 + s4 31 = 141 → −$261,206/141 = −$1,852.
findings.proposed_fix: Take n_trades, avg P&L per trade and win rate from the engine trade log for the portfolio legs (sum of s1c/s3/s4 n_trades; pooled per-trade win rate). Label them 'round-trip trades' and 'win rate (per trade)'. If a daily figure is wanted, add it as a separate row, '% up days'. Test: KPI N Trades == sum of the per-signal table's N Trades.

findings.title: Hard-coded prose on the backtest page (and in README and substack) quotes pre-C21 numbers that contradict the data-driven cards beside it
findings.description: The page headline paragraph and cards say 'S1 ... +$463K, 76% win', 'S1C collapses to −$404K', 'S4 −$189K', 'a single −$333K COVID trade; 2022 −$99K', 'top-5 trades = 73% of profit' and 'positive in 2018/19/21/23/24'. The cards rendered from full_results.pkl on the same page show S1 $693,938, S1C $-599,995 and S4 $-206,437, and methodology row #11 on the same page itself says 'S1 +$463K→+$694K, S1C −$404K→−$600K'. The current trade log gives a worst S1 (COVID) trade of −$299,415, S1 2022 P&L of −$74,007, a top-5 share of 52.5% of net profit, and a positive 2025 as well. The note 'R2 = VOMMA_ACTIVE (deterministic rule: VVIX > 100)' is also stale: the labels use the adaptive rolling 80th-percentile gate, and the fixed 100 threshold disagrees on 19.7% of days. The regime legend's 'R0 Low VIX / backwardation' misstates the rule, which is R0: rv20 > VIX.
findings.evidence: From full_results.pkl all_trades (net_pnl): s1 n=54 total 693,938, win 0.759; worst s1 trades 2020-02-21→03-17 −299,415 and 2018-10-05 −96,788; S1 by exit year {2018: 83k, 2019: 266k, 2020: −198k, 2021: 59k, 2022: −74k, 2023: 308k, 2024: 240k, 2025: 10k}; top-5 = 52.5% of net. The template lines quoted above were found with grep.
findings.proposed_fix: Render these figures from _em (the engine metrics) and a small trade-log summary computed in load_page4 (worst trade, P&L by year, top-5 share) instead of literals. Fix the R2 gate text and the legend. Update README lines 57/59 and substack line 79, or better, generate the README headline block from the same function. Add a test that grep-fails on '$463K' / '$404K' / '$189K' in templates/README, or better, a test asserting that every $-figure in the template comes from d.

findings.title: S3's Sharpe is hidden as 'N/A*' with a false 'ratio diverges' note; the engine value is −5.6 because S3 earns less than T-bills
findings.description: load_page4 overrides S3's Sharpe with 'N/A*'. The footnote says '(mostly flat NAV → near-zero std → ratio diverges)'. The engine's s3_sharpe vs ^IRX is a finite −5.605. The number is strongly negative because S3's 0.32%/yr return is far below the ^IRX hurdle, which averaged 2.40% over the window; T-bills on $1M compound to about +$188K against S3's +$23K. Meanwhile the page tags S3 'POSITIVE' and calls it 'the lone signal positive across every correction'. Hiding the one statistic that shows it losing to cash is a selective presentation.
findings.evidence: full_results.pkl metrics: s3_sharpe=-5.6052, s3_ann_return=0.0032, s3_total_pnl=23212. DB tbill_rates mean over 2018-01-01..2025-03-24 = 2.40% (1,809 rows); cash compounding 18.8% ≈ $187,581 on $1M.
findings.proposed_fix: Show the engine Sharpe (−5.61) with a footnote explaining that it is dominated by the cash hurdle on a mostly-flat NAV, and add an 'excess return vs T-bill' column for every signal. Reword 'lone positive signal' to 'positive gross P&L, but below cash'. Test: signal_metrics S3 Sharpe equals the engine value.

findings.title: The 'Implied − Realised spread' compares VIX with a forecast of E|r|·√252, which on average sits about 22% below realised vol and inflates the spread toward 'premium selling'
findings.description: pdv_model.pkl has horizon=1, so build_xy's target is |r_{t+1}|·√252, a forecast of the annualised mean absolute return. E|r| is about 0.8σ for Gaussian returns and smaller with fat tails. The card labels this 'PDV FORECAST (REALISED)' and subtracts it from VIX (a 30-day σ-type quantity) to headline the 'IMPLIED − REALISED SPREAD' and the 'favours short vol' text. Over 2010-2025 the linear forecast averages 11.45% against a forward 21-day realised vol of 14.77%, so the spread carries a structural upward bias of about 3.3 vol points before any risk premium.
findings.evidence: SPX 2010-2025: E|r|√252=0.1147 vs sqrt(E r²)√252=0.1738 (ratio 0.660). mean(pdv.linear_.predict(features))=0.1145 vs mean(forward 21d RV)=0.1477 (ratio 0.775; median 0.806). pdv.horizon == 1.
findings.proposed_fix: Either (a) refit PDV with horizon=21, whose target is sqrt(mean r²_{t+1..t+21}·252), to match VIX's 30-calendar-day horizon, or (b) rescale the 1-day forecast by the empirical factor mean(RV21)/mean(pred) estimated on the training window only. Label the card 'PDV forecast of 1M realised vol'. Test: on the training sample, mean(forecast)/mean(RV21) is within [0.95, 1.05].

findings.title: Vomma heatmap drops 16 of 69 nodes, including one of the three unstable nodes, because only the first node per 0.05 bin is kept
findings.description: lm_bin = floor(lm/0.05)*0.05, then cell_df.iloc[0]. The 12-15 log-spaced nodes per maturity fall two to a bin in 16 cases, and the second node is discarded. The 365d node at lm=−0.2607 (z=2.05, unstable) shares the −0.30 bin with lm=−0.30 and is hidden, so the heatmap shows 2 red cells while the banner says 3 unstable nodes. The z-score is also pooled across maturities. Vomma scales roughly with √T, so 'unstable' simply marks the longest maturity, which the template's own text admits.
findings.evidence: groupby(['T_days','lm_bin']).size(): 16 cells with 2 nodes. Playwright on the live greeks page: `$$('td.unstable').length == 2`, while the banner says '3 Unstable Nodes'.
findings.proposed_fix: Pivot on the actual node log-moneyness (the grid is already regular per maturity, 15 points), or bin with round() and aggregate by max |z|, marking the cell unstable if any node in it is. Standardise vomma within each maturity (or normalise by vega·√T) before flagging. Test: every row in unstable_nodes appears as a red cell.

findings.title: Every page declares rel=canonical and og:url = homepage, telling search engines the calibration, greeks and backtest pages are duplicates
findings.description: base.html hard-codes <link rel='canonical' href='https://navnoorbawa.me/'> and og:url for all four pages, while freeze_site writes a sitemap listing the four distinct URLs. Google treats canonical as a strong signal to consolidate, so the sub-pages are likely dropped from the index, and shared links to /backtest.html preview as the homepage.
findings.evidence: grep in the frozen output: backtest.html:21, calibration.html:21, greeks.html:21 and index.html:21 all have `<link rel="canonical" href="https://navnoorbawa.me/">`; og:url is identical on all pages.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `{% block canonical %}https://navnoorbawa.me/{% endblock %}` in base.html. Override it per template (e.g. backtest → https://navnoorbawa.me/backtest.html) or derive it from request.path via the ROUTES map, and use it for both og:url and canonical. Test: each frozen page's canonical matches its sitemap entry.

findings.title: Annual returns drop the first trading day of each year (they do not compound to the total), and equity-curve downsampling drops the final 2025-03-24 point
findings.description: ret = g.nav.iloc[-1]/g.nav.iloc[0] − 1 uses the first day of year Y as the base instead of the last close of Y−1, so the return from Dec 31 to the first January session is lost. Chaining the displayed years gives −26.06%, not the −26.12% total. The equity chart uses eq.iloc[::3], which ends on 2025-03-21 and slightly clips extremes (S1 min −1.57% true vs −1.23% shown). At 1,808 points × 5 series the downsampling saves almost nothing.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the previous year's last NAV as the base (nav.resample('YE').last().pct_change(), with the first year based on the initial NAV). Send the full series, or append eq.iloc[[-1]] when downsampling. Test: prod(1+annual) − 1 equals the cumulative return to 1e-10, and eq_dates[-1] equals the parquet end.

findings.title: Dead code in the loaders: Bates unpickled every request and never shown, a PDV R² block that can never run and prints a developer message publicly, and date keys never rendered
findings.description: Computed keys that no template uses: bates, smile_lm/iv/mat, total_loss, feller_pass/binding, pdv_stale, ts_max_date, vix_date, vvix_date, pdv_spread_label, vega_values, scatter_iv, clf_name, variants.s1x/s1s, ann_labels. The PDV 3F/4F R² block needs a 'vix' column that pdv._features never has, so it always takes the else-branch, and the live page shows the developer note 'Active model: PDVLinear3F · PDVLinear4F requires VIX column in stored features.' The 'variants' table (the 'R2-Exit P&L' column) is an approximation (zeroing P&L on R2 days, S1X≈S1RF), not a simulated exit, and is labelled as a result.
findings.evidence: A grep loop over templates returned 0 references for each key listed. The live index text contains 'PDVLinear4F requires VIX column in stored features.' pdv._features.columns has no 'vix'.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the unused computations or render them where intended: pdv_stale and the per-card dates belong in the staleness fix. Remove the R² block or feed it VIX from the DB. Label the variants column 'approx. (P&L zeroed on R2 days)', or compute it from an engine re-run. Test: a lint test listing d keys against template references.

findings.title: Minor security hygiene: Chart.js loaded from a CDN without SRI; the local server binds 0.0.0.0
findings.description: Chart.js 4.4.3 is loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no integrity/crossorigin attributes, so a compromised CDN response would run on the public site. When run locally (no PORT set), app.run binds 0.0.0.0 and exposes the dev server, which also runs the data-mutating refresh threads, to the LAN. Neither is exploitable today; both are standard hardening. (Checked: debug=False, no |safe, autoescape on, tojson for all JS data.)
findings.evidence: base.html:25 `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.4.3/dist/chart.umd.min.js"></script>`; app.py:1435 `app.run(host="0.0.0.0", ...)` with local = not PORT.
findings.proposed_fix: Add integrity='sha384-…' crossorigin='anonymous' (hash of the pinned 4.4.3 file), or vendor chart.umd.min.js into .site-build. Bind 127.0.0.1 when `local` is True. Test: a template test asserting that every external <script> has an integrity attribute.

checked_ok: Importing dashboard/app.py and running freeze_site make no network calls and write nothing under data_store (git status clean after all four loaders and a full freeze). The refresh threads start only under __main__.
debug=False; no |safe filter anywhere; Flask autoescape is active for .html; all JS data goes through |tojson; the JS innerHTML only inserts static strings. No XSS path from data.

Backtest KPIs match the README headline block and the engine metrics: NAV $738,794, P&L −$261,206 (−26.12%), Sharpe −1.799 (engine, vs ^IRX), Sortino −3.280, Max DD −31.54%, DD duration 1729, Ann. return −4.13% (geometric, 252-day years), Calmar −0.131. Per-signal S1/S1C/S3/S4/S2 P&L, Sharpe, win rate and trade counts equal full_results.pkl metrics.
Regime-frequency card is computed from the parquet in the normal path (R0 10.2%, R1 68.0%, R2 21.8% of 4,189 days, 2010–2026), so the C21 fix is correct when the classifier loads.

Feller three-state classification and pinned-parameter count are rendered correctly for the selected fit (margin −1.1e-7 → BINDING; pinned rho, sigma → 3 dof). The kappa half-life formula ln2/κ·252 is correct.

Hard-coded PDV formula (0.354σ1 + 0.241σ2 − 1.496·lev + 0.0346), GARCH β 0.890, persistence 0.979 and half-lives 5/60 match pdv_model.pkl. Classifier top feature fear_premium 39% matches feature_importance(). Quintic texts 2.34 vp, 17.5 vp and ~46 min match quintic_cal (2.3427, 17.53, 2751.8 s).
Sortino uses the correct downside deviation (RMS of min(0, excess) over all days).
Rendered calibration, greeks and backtest pages from my copy are byte-identical to the live navnoorbawa.me pages; index differs only by the (stale) local DB market values.
Live pages render in Chromium with zero console or page errors; all charts instantiate (index 2, calibration 2, greeks 3, backtest 5).
freeze_site: relative-link rewriting leaves no absolute href="/..."; CNAME, .nojekyll, 404, robots and sitemap are written; exits 1 when a route returns 500.
Performance is fine: warm loader times 10–150 ms (cold ~2 s from imports); latest_good_calibration_path ~1 ms over 35 pickles; largest page (backtest) 125 KB.
The selector's ≥3 VIX-tenor gate (C20) correctly excludes all 1-tenor fits from 07-14 to 08-28.
